items.title: Live: Israeli attacks in Lebanon 'blatant violation' of ceasefire, says Iran's president
items.description: Meanwhile, US Donald Trump says if an agreement is not reached, the "shootin' starts bigger and better and stronger than anyone has ever seen before". Follow live.

items.title: Warships 'could absolutely deploy' to Iran if asked, defence chief says
items.description: Australia's chief of defence says Australia could "absolutely" deploy a warship to the Strait of Hormuz if asked by the federal government.

items.title: The Iran war has become a cash cow for the Kremlin
items.description: Donald Trump used to love using the word "winning" but out of the wreckage of the Iran war and the world's oil supplies slowing, there is one man truly winning: Russia's Vladimir Putin.

items.title: Gang rapist on the run after escaping custody at Sydney hospital
items.description: A man convicted of gang raping a 14-year-old girl in a Western Sydney park has escaped from custody while at a hospital. Follow live.

items.title: High Court refuses to hear Bruce Lehrmann's appeal
items.description: The High Court was Bruce Lehrmann's last legal avenue to challenge a Federal Court ruling that found, on the balance of probabilities, he did rape Brittany Higgins.

items.title: People living in vehicles forced to choose between fuel and food
items.description: The high cost of fuel is making it even more difficult for people living in their cars to afford food, electricity and transport.

items.title: Live: Crows get home agains Blues in the wet in Gather Round opener
items.description: The Adelaide Crows send the fans home happy after ending its losing streak by beating Carlton at a packed Adelaide Oval to start Gather Round. Follow live.

items.title: Bulldogs stun misfiring Panthers in big boilover victory
items.description: The Penrith Panthers unbeaten start to the NRL season has been ended in comprehensive fashion by the Bulldogs at Stadium Australia.

items.title: Canavan's rebrand and new Facebook photo, Albanese's Trump rebuke
items.description: With retro shades, big rhetoric and a rejection of net zero, Matt Canavan is hoping to reshape the Nationals. His first big test is just weeks away.

items.title: Grace Tame Foundation announces closure
items.description: The Grace Tame Foundation, established by the Tasmanian-born survivor of child sexual abuse, has announced it is closing because securing funding is becoming "increasingly challenging".

items.title: King Charles writes 'very different' open letter after NT flood disaster
items.description: King Charles has written an open letter to Northern Territory residents following recent devastating flooding, saying the "increasingly catastrophic effects of climate change are surely a siren-call to the world for more urgent action".

items.title: Post-ceasefire attacks in Lebanon spark fears war would get 'much worse'
items.description: As a shaky ceasefire struggles to get under way, deadly Israeli strikes on Lebanon risk worsening the Middle East conflict.

items.title: Is Hormuz open or closed? Shiptracking data reveals true picture
items.description: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has remained at an effective standstill in the 24 hours since Iran conditionally lifted its blockade on the critical shipping lane, amid a fragile ceasefire with the US and Israel.

items.title: Emperor penguins, Antarctic fur seals now endangered due to climate change
items.description: The iconic emperor penguin and the Antarctic fur seal are edging closer to extinction, according to a projection by the world's largest environmental network.

items.title: WA Police launch probe after video shows officer shoving woman to ground during arrest
items.description: An internal police investigation is underway, after video footage emerged online showing a police officer pushing a woman to the ground in Western Australia's far north.

items.title: China's 26 phone calls that brought on a US-Iran ceasefire
items.description: China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi says he held 26 phone calls with his counterparts in Iran, Israel, Russia and Gulf countries before the ceasefire was reached.

items.title: Are you in a de facto relationship without realising?
items.description: Our "ordinary understanding” of de facto relationships may not match up with the legal definition and that can cause big surprises for people in the event of a break-up.

items.title: A wave of low-cost electric trucks is heading for Australia
items.description: Diesel trucks are the backbone of the national supply chain, but figures buried in recent sales data could mark the beginning of the end for these kings of the road.

items.title: Singapore's PM knows Australia is vulnerable but Albanese has leverage
items.description: Anthony Albanese is flying to Singapore as part of a hastily arranged regional mission to shore up crucial fuel supplies, amid warnings the global energy crisis could "sharply turn for the worse".

items.title: Man accused of failing to help his dying wife back behind bars
items.description: Kevin Stanischewski is accused of leaving his wife unconscious for hours after she allegedly told him she had drunk poison.

items.title: Police say 'no evidence of kangaroo strike' in woman's suspicious death
items.description: Northern Territory police say they have been unable to find any evidence of a reported kangaroo strike while investigating a woman's suspicious death on the weekend.

items.title: Uni in financial crisis spent nearly $1.5m on leadership coach, documents show
items.description: Documents released to Four Corners show the University of Technology Sydney spent hundreds of thousands of dollars a year on a leadership coach before planning to slash jobs and courses to save money.

items.title: She hasn't had an injury but $10m horse will never race, heading to retirement instead
items.description: An owner says she has "no regrets" after announcing that the first filly from champion race mare Winx will never race.

items.title: Alcoa rejects mercury emissions concerns from its WA refinery
items.description: The US mining giant says increased mercury emissions from its Wagerup refinery are a by-product of higher production, amid a Conservation Council appeal against its operating licence.

items.title: 'I've got my visa back': Child sex offender allowed to stay in Australia
items.description: The man's permanent visa was automatically cancelled when he was jailed in 2024 for sexually abusing a nine-year-old girl, but a tribunal has upheld his appeal in part due to his "ill health".
